introduction: Texas CEAP helps eligible low-income households with energy costs through local providers. TDHCA does not take individual applications.
description: Texas CEAP helps eligible low-income households with energy costs through local providers. TDHCA does not take individual applications.

sections.who: Local intake assesses household income and energy circumstances under current rules.
sections.get: Utility assistance and education about managing home energy use.
sections.docs:
• Household income records.
  • Energy bill and account details.
  • Disconnection notice if present.
sections.apply:
1. Find local intake

    Choose Utility Bill Payment Help and your location in Help for Texans.

  2. Ask about openings

    Confirm funding and the current checklist.

  3. Submit the application

    Give records to the listed provider.
sections.after: Tell intake about urgent disconnection and contact your supplier about interim arrangements.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using CEAP purpose and administration, Local intake search. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: No. Apply to the local provider identified for your area.
Can a listed provider run out of funds?
Yes. TDHCA warns capacity can prevent assistance.
Is energy education part of CEAP?
The state describes education alongside utility help.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
